transcript: You already have years of lecture decks. Turned into video, they can teach on their own: before class, for revision, or for an online cohort.
Don't start with your whole course. Begin where video helps most, like one assessment explainer. Every student needs it, and it saves you answering the same emails.
A fifty-minute lecture rarely works as one fifty-minute video. Give each concept its own short video, so students can find the part they need later.
Swap dot points for what you'd actually say to a student. Short sentences work better for voices and captions, so check how technical terms are pronounced.
Pick a voice and a slightly slower speed for dense material, turn on captions, and watch it all with sound. Then download the MP4 and add it to your course yourself.
Start with one lecture: one deck and an hour. On Pro, A.I. directs the video, timing each scene to your narration. Try one on Basic at powerpoint2vid.com.
